newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV TO FACE RAFTER IN NEW HAVEN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV TO FACE RAFTER IN NEW HAVEN FINAL.

text.p: Top seed Yevgeny Kafelnikov of Russia mastered former champion Petr Korda 6-4 7-6 (7-4) Saturday to gain the final of the Pilot Pen tennis tournament against Australian Patrick Rafter.
Rafter, the eighth seed, overcame the booming serves of Britain's Greg Rusedski 7-5 4-6 6-3.
There was only one service break in the Kafelnikov-Korda match, that coming in the very first game when the Czech double faulted on the final point.

"That might have been the key to the match because if I took that game I could have put more pressure on him," said Korda. "It seemed like I was fighting for every point -- I had trouble controling the ball."

The match was basically a baseline duel with Korda, the lefthander from the Czech Republic who was the titleholder here in 1991, often in trouble because of unforced errors. He double faulted nine times. Kafelnikov had no double faults.
Kafelnikov, who had come into the match with a 5-2 record against Korda, was down set point for the only time at 5-6 in the second set, but eventually took the game to force the tiebreaker.
In the breaker, Korda started with a double fault but pulled even at 3-3 before backcourt errors cost him the match. Down 5-4, Korda hit one return long, then hit one into the net to end the match.

Korda had saved four match points in the quarter-finals against David Wheaton, but there were no repeat miracles against the sixth-ranked player in the world in a match played in the mid-90s Fahrenheit (mid-30s Celsius).
"The heat really bothered me and it was difficult to move from side to side," said Kafelnikov. "I just wanted to put the ball in play. I was glad it was over in two sets."
The young Russian, who missed more than three months of the tour because of a broken finger, feels he is on the way back. "I'm glad to be on track again. I'm starting to hit the ball well."
Rafter started strongly, taking the first set by breaking Rusedski in the 12th game as he ripped a forehand winner down the line.

The fiery Aussie, however, dropped his serve in the first game of the second set -- the only time in the match he did so -- and that was the opening Rusedski needed to take the set and even the match.
Rafter went ahead 3-0 in the final set and eventually served out the match at love.
"You have to take some chances when you get him down on serve because he's not easy to break," said Rafter.
This is Rafter's fourth final of the year. "I've lost three finals. Now I'd like to win one," he said.
